scenarios.dilemma: Should I accept a job offer in Denver and leave Seattle?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I got a job offer in Denver paying $140k, but my partner Sam works remotely and would have to move with me.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: The offer needs an answer by Friday and the equity vests over four years with a one year cliff.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: A cliff means you could leave with nothing if it ends early. How stable is the company?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: They raised a big round last spring, so I think it is stable enough.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Good. Then the question is what the move costs you outside of money.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Honestly I am scared of leaving my mom, she had surgery last winter and lives twenty minutes from me.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: That sounds heavy. What does she say about it?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: She says go, but she always says that, so I do not trust it.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: It may be worth asking her what she would need to feel supported either way.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I have been meaning to repaint my kitchen, it keeps distracting me from all this.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Update: the salary offer was raised to $155k after I negotiated.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: My lease in Seattle ends in August which gives me a natural exit point.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Sam says they are fine either way but I can tell they are nervous about leaving their friends.

probes.text: Does the vesting schedule make this riskier than I thought?
Who else is affected by this move besides my mom?
What salary are we weighing against staying in Seattle?

scenarios.dilemma: Should I leave my data engineering job for a funded PhD?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I am deciding between a funded PhD in Pittsburgh and staying in my data engineer job at a logistics company.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: The PhD stipend is only $38k and I still owe $22k in student loans.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: That is tight but not impossible. What is the real draw of the program?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: My advisor candidate, Dr. Okafor, studies robotics, which is what I actually care about.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Then the advisor matters more than the school name.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: At work they hinted at a promotion to team lead if I stay through the reorg in spring.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Hints are not offers. Has anything been put in writing?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I play bass in a band on weekends and would hate to lose that.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I think the thing I fear most is regretting never trying the PhD.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Regret is real, but it is not evidence about which path is better.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Fine, but a promotion is concrete and the PhD is not.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Update: Dr. Okafor said she is moving to a university in Texas next year, so the Pittsburgh lab may lose its robotics focus.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: My manager asked me to decide by the end of the month.

probes.text: Is the money even workable on a grad student income?
What was my worry about regret again?
Update: I am now leaning toward the PhD as long as the robotics lab stays.

scenarios.dilemma: Should I quit teaching to open a bakery with my friend Lena?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I want to quit my teaching job to open a small bakery with my friend Lena.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: We have $60k saved and the lease on the Maple Street space is $3,200 a month.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Who is putting in how much of that $60k?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Lena wants to put in only $10k though, so most of the risk is on me.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: How many months of runway would you have if the bakery earned nothing?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: About six months.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: My husband Raj is supportive but his hours at the hospital are unpredictable.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: How does that sit with you when you picture opening day?

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I keep having this dream where the oven breaks on opening day.

timeline.speaker: counselor
timeline.text: Dreams like that often point at what feels out of your control.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Plus my teaching contract renews on May 1st, so I have to tell the school soon.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: I told my sister about it over the weekend and she was thrilled.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.text: Update: Lena agreed to put in $25k instead of $10k.

probes.text: How much of the investment is Lena covering?
Is there a deadline with my school I should plan around?
Given my monthly rent and how long I could last, can I even afford this?
